purpose: Zaleplon is used to help you fall asleep if you have trouble with insomnia. It works very quickly, so it is especially helpful if you have a hard time falling asleep at bedtime or if you wake up in the middle of the night and cannot get back to sleep. It is meant for short-term use only, usually just a few days to a couple of weeks.
how_it_works: Your brain has natural calming signals, and zaleplon helps boost those signals to make you feel sleepy. It works on a specific part of the brain that slows down activity and helps you relax enough to fall asleep. Because it works so fast and leaves your system quickly, you are less likely to feel groggy the next morning compared to some other sleep medications.
common_side_effects: Dizziness, headache, drowsiness, and feeling lightheaded are the most common side effects. Some people notice tingling or numbness, nausea, or memory problems. You might also feel a little uncoordinated right after taking it, which is why you should go straight to bed after your dose.
warnings: Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be alert after taking this medication. Avoid alcohol completely while using zaleplon, as combining them can be very dangerous. Some people have done things like sleepwalking, sleep-driving, or eating while not fully awake — stop the medication and call your doctor if this happens. This medication can be habit-forming, so do not take more than prescribed or use it longer than directed. Tell your doctor if you have a history of depression, breathing problems, or substance use.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 10 mg taken right at bedtime or when you wake up during the night, as long as you still have at least 4 hours left to sleep. Older adults or people with liver problems are often started on a lower dose of 5 mg. Never take more than 20 mg in one night, and only take it when you are ready to go straight to sleep.
